segments.he: מִכְּבָרקדֶם אֶרֶץ-יִשְׂרָאֵל בִּקֵּשׁ אֶחָד אוֹתוֹ עַל בָּנִים וְאָמַר לוֹ שֶׁיִּתֵּן  צְדָקָה,  וְהֵשִׁיב  שֶׁאֵין בִּיכָלְתּוֹ וְאָמַר לוֹ שֶׁיִּהְיֶה לוֹ  אֱמוּנָה,  כִּי  אֱמוּנָה  חָשׁוּב  כִּצְדָקָה.  כְּמוֹ  שֶׁכָּתוּב  בְּאַבְרָהָם (בְּרֵאשִׁית ט"ו): "וְהֶאֱמִין בַּה' וַיַּחְשְׁבֶהָ לּוֹ צְדָקָה". וְאָמַר: שֶׁעַל-יְדֵי אֱמוּנָה  זוֹכֶה  לְבָנִים, כִּי אֱמוּנָה בְּגִימַטְרִיָּא בָּנִים וְכֵן הֲוָה שֶׁנִּפְקַד זֶה הָאִישׁ וְהָיוּ לוֹ בָּנִים:
segments.en: (38.) The moon came to the sun with a complaint — in that the sun performs its main function by day and in summer, while she must function at night and in winter during long cold nights. And the sun was appeasing her — that it would make for her a garment. And they called all the chief tailors [bulshvoy glavna — meaning the great and important ones] to make her a garment. And the lesser tailors also wanted to come — and they said: "Since we are not called, we should not go." And the aforementioned tailors came and replied that it was impossible to take a garment for her — because she is sometimes small...
